37597.subject: Music
37597.question_text:
Define the following musical elements and explain their roles in a musical composition:
(i) Pitch
(ii) Dynamics
(iii) Timbre
(iv) Duration
37597.explanation:
(i) Pitch: The highness or lowness of a sound, determined by the frequency of vibrations. It helps in creating melody and harmony.
(ii) Dynamics: The volume of sound, ranging from soft (piano) to loud (forte). It adds expression and emotional intensity.
(iii) Timbre: The unique quality or color of a sound that distinguishes different instruments or voices.
(iv) Duration: The length of time a sound or silence lasts, forming rhythm and meter in music.

37598.subject: Music
37598.question_text:
Write the following notes in the treble clef:
(i) Middle C
(ii) E above middle C
(iii) G below middle C
(iv) A in the second space of the treble clef.
Also, indicate their respective note values if they are quarter notes.
37598.explanation:
(i) Middle C is written on the first ledger line below the treble clef staff.
(ii) E above middle C is on the first line of the treble clef staff.
(iii) G below middle C is on the second space from the bottom of the treble clef staff.
(iv) A in the second space of the treble clef staff is the note A above middle C.
All notes should be drawn as quarter notes (filled note heads with stems).

37599.subject: Music
37599.question_text: Which of the following scales is characterized by a raised seventh degree when ascending and a lowered seventh degree when descending?
37599.explanation: The Melodic Minor Scale has a raised sixth and seventh degree when ascending and reverts to the natural minor scale (lowered sixth and seventh) when descending.

37600.subject: Music
37600.question_text:
(i) Define interval in music.
(ii) Write the inversion of the following intervals:
(a) Perfect 5th
(b) Major 3rd
(c) Minor 6th
(iii) Explain how the inversion of an interval affects its quality.
37600.explanation:
(i) An interval is the distance between two pitches.
(ii) Inversions:
(a) Perfect 5th inverts to a Perfect 4th.
(b) Major 3rd inverts to a Minor 6th.
(c) Minor 6th inverts to a Major 3rd.
(iii) The inversion of an interval changes its quality (e.g., major becomes minor, perfect remains perfect) and the numerical value is found by subtracting the original interval from 9 (e.g., 5th inverts to 4th: $9 - 5 = 4$).

37601.subject: Music
37601.question_text:
(i) Construct a C Major triad in root position, first inversion, and second inversion.
(ii) Label each inversion correctly.
(iii) Explain how chord inversions are used in harmonic progressions.
37601.explanation:
(i) Root Position: C-E-G
First Inversion: E-G-C
Second Inversion: G-C-E.
(ii) Inversions are labeled based on the lowest note (bass note).
(iii) Chord inversions create smoother voice leading, avoid parallel fifths/octaves, and add variety to harmonic progressions.

37602.subject: Music
37602.question_text: Which cadence is formed by the progression of the dominant chord (V) to the tonic chord (I) and is considered the strongest resolution in tonal music?
37602.explanation: The Perfect Authentic Cadence (V-I) is the strongest resolution in tonal music, providing a sense of finality.

37603.subject: Music
37603.question_text: Discuss three distinctive features of African traditional music, providing examples from Ghanaian music where applicable.
37603.explanation:
(1) Call and Response: A leader sings or plays a phrase, and a group responds (e.g., in Adowa dance music).
(2) Polyrhythm: Multiple rhythms played simultaneously (e.g., in Kpanlogo drumming).
(3) Oral Tradition: Music is transmitted orally, with improvisation and variation (e.g., Fontomfrom drumming).

37604.subject: Music
37604.question_text: Which of the following composers is associated with the Classical Period of Western art music?
37604.explanation: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart is a key composer of the Classical Period (1750–1820), known for his symphonies and operas.

37605.subject: Music
37605.question_text:
Compose an 8-bar melody in the key of G Major for the soprano voice, using:
(i) A clear phrase structure (antecedent and consequent).
(ii) Appropriate rhythmic variety.
(iii) A cadence at the end of each phrase.
37605.explanation:
The melody should:
(1) Start with an antecedent phrase (bars 1–4) ending on a half cadence (V).
(2) Follow with a consequent phrase (bars 5–8) ending on a perfect authentic cadence (V-I).
(3) Use rhythmic variety (e.g., quarter notes, eighth notes, and dotted rhythms).
(4) Stay within the soprano range (G4–G5).

37606.subject: Music
37606.question_text:
You will hear a short melody played twice. Notate the melody in the treble clef, including:
(i) Pitches
(ii) Rhythms
(iii) Key signature (if any)
(iv) Time signature.
Assume the melody is in C Major, 4/4 time, and consists of 4 bars.
37606.explanation:
The melody should be notated accurately based on the aural dictation. Key points:
(1) Correct pitches in C Major.
(2) Rhythms matching the played example (e.g., quarter notes, half notes).
(3) Proper bar lines and time signature (4/4).
(4) No accidentals (since it is in C Major).
